results.quote:
For every fixed \(a\ge b\ge c\ge 0\),

\(\omega(a,b,c)\le\left\{\begin{array}{ c c }
a+b, & c\le\frac{ab}{a+b},\\ \frac{a+b+c}{2}+\frac{1}{4}\left(\frac{ab}{c}+\frac{ac}{b}+\frac{bc}{a}\right), & c>\frac{ab}{a+b}.
\end{array}\right.\) (1)

For every fixed real \(k\ge 0\),

\(\omega(k)\le\left\{\begin{array}{ c c }
2, & 0\le k\le\frac{1}{2},\\ 1+k+\frac{1}{4k}, & k\ge\frac{1}{2}.
\end{array}\right.\) (2)

Consequently \(\omega(k)=2\) for \(0\le k\le\frac{1}{2}\).
The output-size lower bound \(\omega(k)\ge 2\) proves equality for \(0\le k\le\frac{1}{2}\) and hence \(\alpha\ge\frac{1}{2}\).

results.problem: All-pairs shortest paths in directed unweighted graphs
results.quote: Zwick's deterministic algorithm for directed unweighted APSP [15, Section 6] has exponent \(2+\mu\), where \(\omega(\mu)\le 1+2\mu\). Here \(\omega(\frac{1}{2})=2=1+2(\frac{1}{2})\), so it gives _O(n_<sup>2.5</sup>) running time. Combining the full curve with the deterministic (min,+)-product algorithm and APSP reduction of Alman and Vassilevska Williams [1, Theorems 22 and 33-34] further gives _O(n_<sup>2.4999</sup>) running time.
